 Forlan recalls ‘long-standing rivalry’ ahead of Argentina-Uruguay friendly
 Published : 12 November 2026
 • 
 Updated : 12 November 2026, 10:32
 • 
 FOOTBALL
 SHARE 
 Agencies 
 PHOTO: AFP 
 In modern-day football, Argentina-Brazil remains one of the sport's most celebrated rivalries, a battle for South American bragging rights between two neighbours renowned for producing generations of footballing superstars.  
 But Argentina-Uruguay is another historic contest, with roots stretching back more than a century and a rivalry that has lost none of its intensity.
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 That enduring history will add extra significance when Argentina host Uruguay at La Bombonera on Saturday at 5:00am Bangladesh time, even though the encounter is officially a friendly.
 Uruguay interim coach Diego Forlan acknowledged the special nature of the fixture, insisting that the history between the two nations makes it a major challenge regardless of the occasion.
 “However friendly it may be, there’s a rivalry with a long history, and it will be a great challenge,” Forlán said at a press conference on Wednesday.
 The former Uruguay forward welcomed the opportunity to face Lionel Scaloni's side, highlighting Argentina's pedigree as reigning world champions and Copa América holders.
 Image 
 “These kinds of matches are difficult because of the level and prestige of the opponent. When they mentioned the possibility to me, I immediately said yes. It's important to test ourselves,” he added.
 The rivalry dates back to the early 1900s, with the first meeting taking place in 1902. Its most defining chapter came at the inaugural FIFA World Cup final in 1930, when Uruguay defeated Argentina 4-2 in Montevideo to become the first world champions. Since then, encounters between the River Plate neighbours have remained among South America's most eagerly anticipated football contests.
 Forlán also recalled Uruguay's 2-0 victory over Argentina at La Bombonera in November 2023, expressing confidence in his team's ability to produce another strong performance.
 “I envision a great match. If we look back recently, we see a game in which our team played very well,” he said.
 Both camps are dealing with selection concerns ahead of the encounter. Argentina coach Scaloni is monitoring goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez's recovery from jaw surgery, with Gerónimo Rulli ready to step in if the Aston Villa shot-stopper is not cleared to play.
 In midfield, Enzo Fernández and Alexis Mac Allister are expected to feature, while Julián Álvarez and Nicolás Paz are among the likely attacking options. There are also selection battles in defence and on the wings.
 Uruguay, meanwhile, have been boosted by the return of Real Madrid midfielder Federico Valverde. Forlán is still assessing the fitness of Mathías Olivera, who could partner Ronald Araújo in central defence, with Juan Rodríguez another option.
 Darwin Núñez, Rodrigo Bentancur, Lucas Torreira and Giorgian de Arrascaeta are also expected to play important roles for La Celeste.
 After facing Argentina, Uruguay will take on the Dominican Republic, while Scaloni's men will conclude their international window against Costa Rica.
